newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar settles to smooth close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar settles to smooth close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed on its opening on Tuesday, trading calmly and narrowly after Monday's hijinx.
The kiwi closed at 5.15 p.m. (0515 GMT) at US$0.6955/62, slightly up on its 0.6952/59 opening and after trading a 0.6945-61 range.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 68.05 from a 68.11 opening.
Dealers said there was offering interest out of Asia but U.S. investment houses were on the bid.
They said the topside was seen as vulnerable side although 0.6880 was seen by most as a sell.
The TWI is seen comfortable at 68.0 following the Reserve Bank's surprise firming signal on Monday.

There was interest in comments from Finance Minister Bill Birch who in an interview with Reuters Financial Television in Japan said the RB's signal was sent because of the rapidity of the change in monetary adjustment.
